assistant_message.content:
### मेरी सलाह

ई-कॉमर्स प्लेटफॉर्म को अपने Grievance Officer की संपर्क जानकारी दिखानी होती है। अधिकारी को शिकायत **48 घंटे में स्वीकार** करनी और मिलने के **एक महीने के भीतर** उसका निपटारा करना होता है। [1](#cite-1)

### अगर इससे बात न बने

अगर Grievance Officer जवाब न दे, शिकायत बंद कर दे या केवल इंतज़ार करने को कहे, तो **1915** पर कॉल करें या National Consumer Helpline पोर्टल पर शिकायत दर्ज करें। यह अदालत जाने से पहले का शिकायत मंच है; वहाँ भी समाधान न हो तो District Consumer Commission में e-Jagriti के जरिए औपचारिक शिकायत की जा सकती है। ऐसी उपभोक्ता शिकायत सामान्यतः कारण पैदा होने के **दो वर्ष के भीतर** करनी होती है। [2](#cite-2)[3](#cite-3)[4](#cite-4)

### ये चीज़ें तैयार रखें

अपने पास ऑर्डर की रसीद, भुगतान रिकॉर्ड, गलत सामान की फोटो यदि उपलब्ध हो, वापसी या पिकअप संदेश, ट्रैकिंग स्थिति और कस्टमर केयर चैट की तारीख वाली प्रतियां रखें। मूल रिकॉर्ड न बदलें। चाहें तो मैं इन्हीं तथ्यों से Grievance Officer या NCH के लिए छोटी शिकायत लिख दूँ।

### एक बात बताइए

क्या यह खरीद भारत में हुई थी, और आपने सामान किस तारीख को लौटाया था?

sources.title: Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020
sources.locator: Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, Rule 4(4)-(5), Gazette pages 3-4
sources.text:
Under Rule 4(4)–(5) of the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, every e-commerce entity must appoint a grievance officer, display their contact mechanism, acknowledge consumer complaints within 48 hours, and redress the complaint within one month from receipt; if the platform's Grievance Officer has already been contacted and failed to resolve or redirected the consumer back to ordinary support, internal escalation is exhausted and the consumer should escalate externally to the National Consumer Helpline (1915) or Consumer Commission.

Exact official passage: An e-commerce entity must maintain a grievance-redress mechanism and display the grievance officer's details. Rule 4 states that the officer must acknowledge a consumer complaint within forty-eight hours and redress it within one month from receipt.
sources.limitations: Notified 23-Jul-2020 (read with 2020 corrigendum and Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Amendment Rules, 2021); verify official Gazette commencement before relying on any later draft or proposed amendment. Where internal Grievance Officer escalation has already been attempted without resolution, do not send the user back to internal support—advance to NCH (1915) / e-Jagriti. Exceptions: Does not automatically guarantee a refund where underlying physical return/pickup facts are disputed; If the user already emailed/contacted the Grievance Officer and was redirected or closed without redress, internal Rule 4 escalation is already attempted—recommend National Consumer Helpline (1915 / consumerhelpline.gov.in) next Treatment: in_force_with_2021_amendment.

sources.title: National Consumer Helpline About
sources.text: The National Consumer Helpline (NCH) is a single point of access for consumers across India for grievance redressal at the pre-litigation stage. Consumers can register grievances in 17 languages by calling the toll-free number 1915 or through the web portal consumerhelpline.gov.in. The portal provides an alternate dispute redressal mechanism before litigation; it does not guarantee a refund or a remedy.
sources.limitations: Official operational information checked on 20 November 2026; not a guarantee of refund or resolution. Incident-specific legal eligibility still requires assessment.

sources.title: National Consumer Helpline (1915 / consumerhelpline.gov.in) — Department of Consumer Affairs
sources.locator: About National Consumer Helpline — Portal questions 1, 8 and 9 (Toll-Free 1915)
sources.text:
When platform customer support and the platform's Grievance Officer have already closed, ignored, or redirected a consumer refund/return dispute (such as a disputed multi-item pickup where physical collection and system return records differ), the immediate external pre-litigation next step is filing a grievance on the National Consumer Helpline (NCH — toll-free 1915 or https://consumerhelpline.gov.in), which forwards the dispute to convergence companies with a typical up-to-30-day resolution window; if still unresolved, file a formal complaint before the District Consumer Commission via e-Jagriti (https://e-jagriti.gov.in/).

Exact official passage: The National Consumer Helpline portal is a pre-litigation grievance mechanism. It forwards grievances to the concerned company, agency, regulator or ombudsman. It does not guarantee a remedy. If the grievance is not resolved to the consumer's satisfaction, the consumer may approach the appropriate Consumer Commission. The portal says the process may take up to 30 days to reach a logical conclusion.
sources.limitations: Official Department of Consumer Affairs pre-litigation mechanism; formal adjudication and enforceable refund/compensation orders lie with District/State/National Consumer Commissions via e-Jagriti under CPA 2019 (Section 35 / Section 69 two-year limitation). Exceptions: NCH is pre-litigation assistance, not a court, and filing on NCH does not pause the two-year statutory limitation under Section 69 CPA 2019 Treatment: official_guidance_verified.

sources.title: Consumer Protection Act, 2019 — Sections 35 & 69 (India Code)
sources.text:
Under Sections 35 and 69 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, if internal grievance redress and National Consumer Helpline pre-litigation efforts do not resolve a consumer deficiency or disputed refund, a consumer may file a formal complaint before the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (electronically through https://e-jagriti.gov.in/) where paid consideration does not exceed Rs. 50 lakh, within two years from the date the cause of action arose.

Exact official passage: A complaint, in relation to any goods sold or delivered or agreed to be sold or delivered or any service provided or agreed to be provided, may be filed with a District Commission by the consumer... The District Commission, the State Commission or the National Commission shall not admit a complaint unless it is filed within two years from the date on which the cause of action has arisen.
sources.limitations: Pecuniary jurisdiction revised by Consumer Protection (Jurisdiction of the District Commission, the State Commission and the National Commission) Rules, 2021 (District Commission up to Rs. 50 lakh paid consideration); online filing administered via e-Jagriti. Exceptions: Pure employer-employee unpaid salary disputes are employment matters, not consumer disputes under CPA 2019 Treatment: in_force_with_2021_2023_rules.
